header.stance: 油價與核心通膨，使7月緊縮更迫近

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價大漲，Waller再提近期升息可能

美伊再次交火，加上荷莫茲貨運收費提案推升油價，美債週一走弱。Christopher Waller又提出更迫近的政策風險：若核心通膨再次偏熱，Fed可能需要考慮近期緊縮。市場反映的7月升息機率，由盤中稍早不到40%提高至接近50%。

5年期殖利率領升7個基點至4.37%，2年期達4.26%，10年期達4.62%，指標券升幅主要來自實質利率。Waller的疑慮不只在能源，也包含原本就存在的核心物價壓力，使下一次CPI與Kevin Warsh就任主席後首度國會聽證，成為升息時間表能否提前的關鍵。

原油漲逾9%，科技股重挫、美元走強，貨幣市場卻相對平穩：大額國庫券標售有充足投標，隔夜擔保融資利率仍偏低。企業繼續透過專案融資、證券化與其他結構取得資金，但基準利率升高，也提高了使用這些管道的成本。

## CPI與Warsh聽證前，中天期美債跌幅最大

2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.26%，5年期上升7個基點至4.37%，10年期上升6個基點至4.62%，30年期上升4個基點至5.10%。升幅不一，使2年與10年期利差擴大1個基點至36，2年與30年期利差卻收窄1個基點至84。5年期表現最弱，反映的不只是可能即將升息，也包括緊縮延續超過一次會議的風險。

10年期實質殖利率上升4個基點至2.36%，損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點至2.26%。5年與7年期實質殖利率各上升4個基點，至2.06%及2.20%；20年與30年期各上升3個基點，至2.69%及2.89%。油價提高了預期通膨成本，投資人對各天期要求的實質報酬也同步增加。

Waller表示，若再有一次強勁核心通膨，FOMC可能必須討論近期緊縮。截至5月，核心PCE年增率已達3.4%；關稅、能源與AI基礎設施需求增加壓力，消費仍有韌性，就業也穩定。他希望看到連續幾個月較低數字，才能確認改善。因此，單月偏弱資料帶來的安心程度，可能不如另一次偏熱資料對升息理由的強化。

不過，Waller也認為通膨預期仍穩定，勞動市場不如2021至2022年緊俏；核心物價若持續放緩，仍可支持利率不變。Warsh尚未提出完整經濟看法或利率預測，這次聽證除了說明如何解讀資料，也將呈現他打算如何帶領決策。

### 政策定價轉緊，大額國庫券仍有買盤

4週與6週期國庫券殖利率各上升1個基點至3.70%，8週期維持3.72%；3個月上升5個基點至3.85%，6個月上升4個基點至4.00%，一年期上升6個基點至4.12%。最短現金天期之外的升幅更大，與預期政策改變一致。

財政部發行$920億91天期國庫券，最高利率3.760%，投標倍數2.84；間接、直接投標人與交易商分別取得56.76%、8.24%及34.99%。約$790億182天期最高利率3.860%，投標倍數3.11；間接投標人取得66.49%，直接投標人8.09%，交易商25.42%。兩券均於7月16日交割。

紐約Fed在截至8月13日的每月操作期間，將準備金管理用途的國庫券購買維持約$100億，另計畫約$176億再投資。7月8日準備金為$3.14兆，現金充足使隔夜擔保融資利率低於準備金利率。接下來國庫券供給，以及預期超過$1兆的財政部現金餘額，都可能抽走準備金，但週一的政策賣壓尚未演變成融資吃緊。

## 信用融資走向無擔保債以外，風險也隨結構改變

美債殖利率上升，LQD下跌0.47%、HYG下跌0.24%、JNK下跌0.18%，高收益跌幅遠小於科技股。借款人仍能取得資金，但AI融資成長，正使更多信用曝險移出傳統大型雲端業者的無擔保債市場。

單一發行人額度與反覆供給，讓投資人更挑剔。資料中心結構把租戶付款納入擔保資產，擴大買方來源，也要求貸款人評估租約持續性、租戶付款能力、完工、電力供應與運轉穩定性。即使科技公司名稱熟悉，這些資產層級問題仍須個別分析。

RBC已開始為美元單一名稱CDS造市，並計畫推出歐元合約，擴大信用衍生品交易。銀行表示6月單一名稱交易明顯增加，信用指數選擇權量則較去年同期翻倍。科技業者發債增加之際，新合約與組合工具可供投資人避險，或表達相對價值看法。

Robinhood正測試至少$4億、分四部分的信用卡應收款證券需求，規模可能增加至$5億，最高評等部分初步利差約為指標加80個基點。交易由Wells Fargo與Barclays承辦，底層品牌卡帳戶由Coastal Community Bank持有。今年信用卡擔保證券已籌逾$110億，包括Capital One的$38.5億交易，顯示這類應收款仍有專門買盤。

Pinewood則為可能發行的固定利率英鎊債舉辦投資人會議，評等跨越高收益與投資級：標普BB-、Fitch BBB-。既有債務包括£7.5億、票息6%、2030年到期票據，以及£3億、2027年11月到期票據。交易仍在行銷階段，定價須反映營運信用與到期結構。

### Aquarion公營化，水費決策成為債權人關注重點

Aquarion Water Authority計畫7月14日發行$24億債券，包括$18.3億A-優先債及$5.472億BBB+次順位債。主管機關3月核准後，該機構已於6月底完成向Eversource收購水務公司。此次融資支應已完成的所有權變更，以及公用事業資本需求。

系統服務22萬戶，預計明年水費調漲略逾8%，之後至2035年每年漲逾6%。公有體制可使用成本較低的免稅債，但水費決定權也由州監理機關，轉至59位地方官員與一位州長指定代表組成的董事會。債權人仰賴董事會落實足以支應本息與建設的調漲；免稅融資的優勢，背後仍有治理與民眾負擔能力的考驗。

紐約收盤後，巴西Oncoclinicas正準備庭外重整，希望減記債務，但不將債權轉為股權。其負債全為本幣，並無全球債券。公司先前積極擴張，如今與其他巴西醫療集團一樣，走向重整或出售資產。本幣融資避免了借款幣別錯配，卻無法阻止槓桿與整併壓力超過營運現金的承受能力。

## 日本退休基金配置不變，日債失去潛在新增買盤

媒體報導GPIF並無大幅調整配置的計畫，日本因此反轉週五有利債市的訊號。日圓盤中最多貶值0.4%至每美元162.36，日債跌勢延續。這個規模約$1.8兆的基金，在2025年3月檢討時，仍保留本地債券、本地股票、海外債券與海外股票各四分之一配置。策略變更須經正式受託管理程序，限制了資金立即依政治意向轉向的可能。

沒有退休基金快速增持，日債仍須面對龐大公共支出、弱勢匯率，以及日本央行正常化是否落後通膨的疑慮。另一方面，配置不變也避免海外資產目標立即下調。眼前日債下跌提高了全球殖利率比較基準，日本海外需求的長期方向則仍未明朗。

歐元區預測顯示另一種限制。荷莫茲再受阻、能源供應受威脅，經濟學家把2026年成長預測中位數由0.7%降至0.5%，低於ECB的0.8%基準；通膨預測仍為2.8%，並預期9月再次升息。相同供給衝擊既拖累活動、又推高價格，使弱成長對債券的支撐較有限。

美國美東14:00公布的財政報告，則補充了籌資需求。6月赤字$1,203億，去年同期為盈餘$270億，收入下降、支出上升。財政年度迄今赤字達$1.367兆，淨利息$8,272億，向公眾借款$1.340兆。數字在下午強化了結構性供給負擔；稍早由中天期領跌的行情，已先受到油價與Waller政策警告影響。

## 印尼保住評等，美元與油價仍提高新興市場成本

美元指數上漲0.31%至101.28，美國實質殖利率也提高，EMB下跌0.64%。硬通貨借款人同時面對較高基準折現率與較強美元，油價衝擊則進一步區分進口國與出口國。

標普維持印尼BBB與穩定展望，肯定GDP 3%的赤字上限及財政紀律紀錄。在穆迪與Fitch先前將展望轉負後，這消除了立即降評威脅。免費餐食預算的削減計畫有助維持財政限制，但印尼盾今年跌近8%，仍使進口通膨與信心受到關注。

評等結果未能逆轉所有市場跌幅。印尼10年期美元債下跌0.4美分至100.9，本幣債收復部分跌勢，股票則收高。投資人肯定財政保障，同時仍須承受更不利的外部環境。

智利雖擴大借款計畫，美元融資利差仍很低。自3月底以來收窄24個基點至82，接近2007年水準。參議院授權增加$62億借款，財政部計畫今年剩餘時間發行$52億國際債；先前申請的借款量，已比原計畫多36%。經濟活動連續五個月年減，結構性財政餘額目標也放寬。能源幾乎全仰賴進口，使荷莫茲中斷更可能干擾籌資執行。

肯亞考慮在截至2027年6月的財政年度內，買回最高$5億國際債，以新美元債提供資金，將是兩年內第四次類似操作。截至3月底，外債合計$437億，其中國際債投資人持有$106億；償債支出超過醫療與教育。平滑到期分布可減少短期集中壓力，卻不會增加可用於還款的收入。

### 通膨限制本地降息空間

衣索比亞將基準利率由15%提高至16%，為這項利率制度建立後首次升息，同時取消銀行信貸每年成長24%的上限。5月通膨已達13.4%，預期未來六個月仍為兩位數；數量限制解除之際，政策利率則收緊。

印度6月CPI年增率由3.93%升至4.38%，食品通膨由4.78%升至5.32%，農村4.74%也高於城市3.92%。能源風險回升之際，物價加速限制了本地債市喘息空間。

Standard Chartered將奈及利亞2026年通膨預測由12%調高至15.5%，預期今年僅降息150個基點，政策利率由目前26.5%降至25%，這是該行對後續政策的預估。央行通膨感受指數由44.8升至45，能源、治安、融資成本與匯率被列為壓力來源。在預期原本就難穩定的地方，燃料成本可能使降息更慢。

## 原油漲逾9%，科技股與黃金同步下跌

再次交火與荷莫茲貨物20%收費提案，使WTI上漲9.42%至$78.14，布蘭特上漲9.59%至$83.30。按目前油價估計，一艘滿載超大型油輪可能須付約$3,200萬。執行細節仍不清楚，但大幅提高航運費用的可能，已重新推升燃料成本疑慮。

S&P 500下跌0.79%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.88%，半導體下跌4.78%。韓國晶片跌勢延伸至美國，SK Hynix美國存託股份下跌9.3%；VIX上升14.17%至17.16。科技同時承受較高折現率與產業本身的壓力，跌幅遠大於整體高收益債。

地緣風險升高，黃金期貨卻下跌2.61%至$3,997，較高實質殖利率與較強美元壓過避險需求。投資人考慮Fed可能如何回應通膨，債券與黃金因而同跌，沒有出現經濟活動突然崩落時常見的保護性買盤。

影響能持續多久仍是關鍵。荷莫茲成本若長期提高，重估可能擴散至週一能源與科技之外；即使物流恢復，Waller對核心通膨的另一層疑慮，仍使利率前景取決於新資料，而不只是原油。

## 先看CPI與Warsh，再看現金供給與日債需求

6月CPI與實質所得將於7月14日美東08:30公布，Warsh於10:00赴眾議院作證；PPI及參議院聽證在7月15日。核心與服務細項，將檢驗Waller所說的風險：最新能源衝擊，是否正在放大原本已存在的通膨問題。7月升息定價接近50%之際，主席如何解讀，可能與市場對整體數字的即時反應同樣重要。

財政部7月14日美東11:30發行$950億42天期國庫券，週一3個月與6個月券則於7月16日交割，當天16:30再公布H.4.1。投標、擔保融資與準備金，將顯示財政部重建現金餘額時，市場吸收供給是否順暢。Aquarion計畫7月14日的地方政府債發行，另可觀察投資人對大額新公營信用及其水費承諾的接受程度。

日本7月14日約¥7,000億20年期標售，將測試GPIF預期落空後的需求；歐元區7月15日工業生產，則補充成長預測轉弱後的實際活動。日債投標與後續交易可顯示其他買方是否補上退休基金未立即增持的空間，歐洲產出則有助判斷較慢成長能抵銷多少持續能源通膨。

overall_summary.headline: 原油大漲，Waller警告推升7月升息機率至近50%
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美伊再度交火，加上荷莫茲貨物20%收費提案，原油漲逾9%。Waller警告，核心通膨若再次偏熱，可能需要近期升息，7月機率由不到40%提高至近50%。5年期殖利率上升7個基點至4.37%，10年期實質殖利率上升4個基點至2.36%。

$920億3個月及約$790億6個月國庫券都有充足投標，隔夜擔保融資仍偏低。資料中心結構、CDS避險與消費應收款，繼續擴大信用管道；Aquarion計畫中的$24億發債則帶來另一風險：新公營水務機構能否落實水費調漲。

GPIF並無大幅配置調整計畫的報導，使日本退休基金題材的漲勢反轉。標普維持印尼評等，智利與肯亞則在較強美元下，尋求增加或替換融資。市場對Fed急迫性已明顯提高，接下來由CPI與Warsh聽證檢驗。
overall_summary.summary: 5年期美債殖利率上升7個基點至4.37%，10年期達4.62%，實質利率主導指標券跌勢。國庫券投標仍強，政策衝擊尚未變成眼前融資緊縮。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil Surges as Waller Puts a Near-Term Hike Back in Play

Treasuries sold off Monday after renewed US-Iran strikes and a proposed Hormuz cargo charge sent oil sharply higher. Christopher Waller added a more immediate policy risk: another hot core-inflation reading could require the Fed to consider tightening soon. Markets lifted the implied chance of a July increase to nearly 50%, from below 40% earlier in the session.

Five-year yields led the move, rising 7 basis points to 4.37%. The two-year reached 4.26% and the 10-year 4.62%, with real yields accounting for most of the benchmark increase. Waller's concern extended beyond energy to underlying inflation, making the next CPI release and Kevin Warsh's first congressional testimony as chair pivotal for the newly accelerated rate outlook.

Oil gained more than 9%, technology shares fell sharply and the dollar strengthened. Money markets were calmer: large bill auctions drew substantial demand and overnight secured funding remained soft. Corporate borrowing continued through project finance, securitization and other structures, but higher base rates increased the cost of reaching those investors.

## The Belly Leads Losses Before CPI and Warsh's Testimony

Two-year Treasury yields rose 5 basis points to 4.26%, five years added 7 to 4.37%, 10 years increased 6 to 4.62% and 30 years gained 4 to 5.10%. The uneven move widened 2s10s by 1 basis point to 36 but narrowed 2s30s by 1 to 84. Five-year underperformance captured the combination of a possible imminent hike and restraint lasting beyond a single meeting.

Ten-year real yield rose 4 basis points to 2.36%, while breakeven inflation increased 2 to 2.26%. Five- and seven-year real yields each added 4 to 2.06% and 2.20%; 20 and 30 years gained 3 to 2.69% and 2.89%. Oil increased expected inflation costs, but investors also demanded a higher real return throughout the curve.

Waller said another strong core reading could put near-term tightening before the FOMC. Core PCE was already up 3.4% in the year through May, with tariffs, energy and AI infrastructure demand adding pressure while consumer spending remained resilient and employment stable. He wanted several months of lower readings to establish improvement. One benign release would therefore provide less reassurance than another firm report would add to the case for action.

He also described inflation expectations as well anchored and labor conditions as less tight than in 2021–22. Sustained core moderation could still justify holding rates. Warsh had not yet supplied a detailed economic view or rate projection, leaving his testimony important both for interpreting the data and for explaining how he would lead that decision.

### Large Bill Sales Find Buyers Despite Higher Policy Pricing

Four- and six-week bill yields each rose 1 basis point to 3.70%, while eight weeks held at 3.72%. Three months added 5 to 3.85%, six months 4 to 4.00% and one year 6 to 4.12%. The larger moves beyond the shortest cash maturities followed the change in expected policy.

Treasury sold $92 billion of 91-day bills at a 3.760% high rate with 2.84 bid-to-cover. Indirect, direct and dealer shares were 56.76%, 8.24% and 34.99%. The approximately $79 billion 182-day sale cleared at 3.860% with 3.11 coverage; indirects took 66.49%, directs 8.09% and dealers 25.42%. Both settle July 16.

The New York Fed kept reserve-management bill purchases near $10 billion for the monthly period ending August 13 and planned about $17.6 billion of reinvestments. Reserves were $3.14 trillion on July 8, and secured overnight financing traded below interest on reserve balances amid abundant cash. The approaching bill supply and a Treasury cash balance expected to exceed $1 trillion could withdraw reserves, but Monday's policy selloff had not become a funding squeeze.

## Credit Expands Beyond Unsecured Bonds, With Different Risks Attached

LQD fell 0.47%, HYG 0.24% and JNK 0.18% as Treasury yields rose. High-yield losses were far smaller than the technology-equity decline. Borrowers retained access, although the growth of AI financing was pushing more credit outside the conventional unsecured hyperscaler market.

Single-issuer limits and repeated supply were making investors more selective. Data-center structures bring tenant lease payments into the collateral pool, broadening the buyer base while requiring lenders to assess lease durability, tenant capacity, completion, power access and uptime. A familiar technology name alone cannot answer those asset-level questions.

RBC had begun making markets in dollar single-name CDS and planned euro contracts as it expanded credit-derivatives trading. The bank reported sharply higher single-name activity in June and credit-index option volume double the year-earlier level. New contracts and baskets offer ways to hedge or express relative value as technology issuers bring more bonds to market.

Robinhood was testing demand for at least $400 million of credit-card receivables bonds in four parts, potentially increasing to $500 million. Initial talk for the highest-rated tranche was around 80 basis points over the benchmark. Wells Fargo and Barclays ran the transaction, with Coastal Community Bank owning the underlying branded-card accounts. Dedicated receivables buyers had already taken more than $11 billion of card-backed issuance that year, including Capital One's $3.85 billion sale.

Pinewood held investor meetings for a possible fixed-rate sterling bond. Ratings straddled high yield and investment grade: BB- at S&P and BBB- at Fitch. Existing debt included a £750 million 6% note due 2030 and a £300 million note maturing in November 2027. The marketing was a prospective financing, with pricing still dependent on the operating credit and maturity profile.

### Aquarion's New Public Ownership Shifts the Rate-Setting Risk

Aquarion Water Authority planned a $2.4 billion bond sale for July 14, including $1.83 billion of A- senior debt and $547.2 million of BBB+ subordinate bonds. The authority's acquisition of the water company from Eversource had closed at the end of June after regulatory approval in March. The financing would fund that completed change of ownership alongside the utility's capital needs.

Customers faced increases of a little over 8% next year, followed by more than 6% annually through 2035. The system serves 220,000 customers. Public ownership permits lower-cost tax-exempt borrowing, but rate-setting would move from state regulators to a board of 59 municipal officials and one gubernatorial appointee. Bondholders depended on that board implementing the increases needed for debt service and construction. The attraction of tax exemption came with a concrete governance and affordability test.

After the NY close, Brazil's Oncoclinicas was preparing an out-of-court restructuring seeking a debt haircut without converting creditors into shareholders. Liabilities were entirely local-currency, with no global bonds. The move followed aggressive expansion and other Brazilian healthcare restructurings and asset sales. Domestic-currency funding avoided a borrowing-currency mismatch, but could not prevent leverage and consolidation from overwhelming operating cash generation.

## Japan's Pension Reversal Removes a Prospective Bond Buyer

Japan reversed Friday's favorable duration signal after a report that no GPIF allocation overhaul was planned. The yen weakened as much as 0.4% to 162.36 per dollar and JGBs extended losses. The roughly $1.8 trillion fund had retained equal quarter allocations to domestic bonds, domestic equities, foreign bonds and foreign equities at its March 2025 review. Strategic changes require a formal fiduciary process, limiting the prospect of an immediate politically directed shift.

Without a rapid increase in pension demand, Japanese bonds still faced ambitious public spending, a weak currency and concern that BOJ normalization was lagging inflation. Keeping the allocation unchanged also avoided an immediate cut in the foreign-asset target. JGB losses raised the near-term global yield hurdle, while the longer-run direction of Japanese overseas demand remained unresolved.

Euro-area forecasts showed a different constraint. Economists cut median 2026 growth to 0.5% from 0.7%, below the ECB's 0.8% baseline, as renewed Hormuz disruption threatened energy supply. Inflation was still forecast at 2.8%, with another rate increase expected in September. Weaker activity offered less support for bonds when the same supply shock kept prices elevated.

The US fiscal statement, released at 14:00 ET, added detail on borrowing needs. June recorded a $120.3 billion deficit versus a $27.0 billion surplus a year earlier, as receipts fell and outlays rose. The fiscal-year-to-date deficit reached $1.367 trillion, net interest $827.2 billion and borrowing from the public $1.340 trillion. These figures reinforced the structural supply burden during the afternoon; the earlier belly-led selloff had already followed oil and Waller's policy warning.

## Indonesia Keeps Its Rating as the Dollar and Oil Raise EM Funding Costs

EMB fell 0.64% as DXY rose 0.31% to 101.28 and US real yields increased. Hard-currency borrowers faced both a higher benchmark discount rate and a firmer dollar. The oil shock added a separate divide between importers and exporters.

S&P affirmed Indonesia at BBB with a stable outlook, citing the 3% of GDP deficit ceiling and a record of fiscal discipline. That removed an immediate downgrade threat after Moody's and Fitch turned their outlooks negative. Planned cuts to the free-meals budget supported the fiscal limit, although a rupiah down almost 8% for the year kept imported inflation and confidence in focus.

The rating decision did not reverse all market losses. Indonesia's 10-year dollar bond fell 0.4 cents to 100.9, while local bonds recovered part of their decline and equities closed higher. Investors welcomed the fiscal assurance against a more difficult external backdrop.

Chile still enjoyed unusually tight dollar pricing despite an increased borrowing plan. Its spread had narrowed 24 basis points since end-March to 82, near 2007 levels. The Senate authorized another $6.2 billion of borrowing, and the Finance Ministry planned $5.2 billion of international issuance over the rest of the year after seeking 36% more debt than initially planned. Activity had contracted annually for five months and the structural-balance target had been relaxed. Near-total dependence on imported energy made execution more vulnerable to Hormuz disruption.

Kenya considered buying back up to $500 million of Eurobonds in the fiscal year ending June 2027, financed by new dollar debt. It would be the fourth such exercise in two years. External debt totaled $43.7 billion at end-March, including $10.6 billion owed to Eurobond investors, while debt service exceeded health and education spending. Smoother maturities could reduce a near-term concentration without increasing the revenue available to repay debt.

### Inflation Constrains Local Easing

Ethiopia raised its benchmark to 16% from 15%, the first increase since the rate was introduced, while removing a 24% annual bank-credit growth cap. Inflation had reached 13.4% in May and was expected to remain in double digits for the next six months. The policy rate tightened as the quantitative lending restriction was lifted.

India's June CPI accelerated to 4.38% from 3.93%. Food inflation rose to 5.32% from 4.78%, and rural inflation of 4.74% exceeded the 3.92% urban pace. The increase limited room for local-duration relief as energy risk returned.

Standard Chartered raised its Nigerian 2026 inflation forecast to 15.5% from 12% and expected only 150 basis points of easing, taking the policy rate to 25% from 26.5%. The central bank's inflation-perception index increased to 45 from 44.8, with energy, insecurity, financing costs and the exchange rate identified as pressures. Fuel costs threatened to slow easing where expectations were already difficult to stabilize.

## Oil Jumps More Than 9% as Technology Shares and Gold Fall

WTI rose 9.42% to $78.14 and Brent gained 9.59% to $83.30 after renewed strikes and the proposed 20% charge on cargo crossing Hormuz. At prevailing prices, the payment was estimated at about $32 million for a fully loaded very large crude carrier. Details of implementation remained unclear, but the prospect of a much higher shipping bill revived concern over fuel costs.

The S&P 500 fell 0.79%, Nasdaq 100 1.88% and semiconductors 4.78%. SK Hynix's American depositary shares lost 9.3% as the Korean chip selloff carried into US trading. VIX rose 14.17% to 17.16. Technology faced both the higher discount rate and a sector-specific decline, with much larger losses than broad high-yield debt.

Gold futures fell 2.61% to $3,997 despite heightened geopolitical risk. Higher real yields and a stronger dollar outweighed haven demand. Bonds and bullion both weakened as investors considered a Fed response to inflation, rather than buying them as protection against a sudden collapse in activity.

Persistence remained the key uncertainty. A lasting Hormuz cost shock could spread beyond Monday's energy and technology repricing. If flows normalized, Waller's separate concern about core inflation would still leave the rate outlook dependent on the next data rather than oil alone.

## CPI and Warsh Come First; Cash Supply and JGB Demand Follow

June CPI and real earnings arrive July 14 at 08:30 ET, followed by Warsh's House testimony at 10:00. PPI and his Senate appearance follow July 15. Core and services detail will test Waller's warning that the latest energy shock is amplifying an existing inflation problem. With July hike pricing near 50%, the chair's interpretation will matter as much as any immediate response to the headline number.

Treasury sells $95 billion of 42-day bills July 14 at 11:30 ET. Monday's three- and six-month bills settle July 16, ahead of that day's H.4.1 release at 16:30. Auction demand, secured funding and reserves will show how easily cash absorbs supply as Treasury rebuilds its balance. Aquarion's planned municipal sale July 14 provides a separate test of demand for a large new public-credit name and its rate-setting commitments.

Japan's roughly ¥700 billion 20-year auction July 14 will test demand after the GPIF disappointment. Euro-area industrial production follows July 15, adding realized activity to the weaker growth forecasts. JGB bidding and post-auction trading will reveal whether other buyers offset the absence of an immediate pension shift; European output will help gauge how far slower growth can counter continued energy inflation.
